facts.raw_span: a 1½-week history of headache and blurred vision
MRI of the brain demonstrated a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect
HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
an HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL
Serum toxoplasma IgG was elevated
CSF studies showed 48 cells/µL (97% lymphocytes) with positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii (286 copies/mL)
Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
fever to 39.6 °C
generalized weakness
a 1-day history of productive cough
Chest radiograph showed a new left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence
CT scan of the chest confirmed extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates with focal consolidation in the left upper lobe

concepts.why: The patient has a ring-enhancing lesion in the brain, elevated toxoplasma IgG, and positive DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii, which are all consistent with toxoplasmosis.

The patient has a new left upper lobe opacification, diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence, and extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates, which are all consistent with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, especially in the context of HIV infection and low CD4 count.
The patient has a confirmed HIV infection with a low CD4 count and high viral load.
The patient has a ring-enhancing lesion in the brain, elevated toxoplasma IgG, and positive DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii, which are all consistent with cerebral toxoplasmosis.

The patient has a fever, generalized weakness, and productive cough, which could be consistent with immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome, especially in the context of HIV infection and recent initiation of antiretroviral therapy.

rationales.F02: Ring-enhancing lesion in the brain is highly suggestive of cerebral toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F05: Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG is a strong indicator of toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F06: Positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF is diagnostic of cerebral toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F07: Histopathologic examination revealing bradyzoites and tachyzoites is diagnostic of toxoplasmosis.
rationales.F11: Reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates with focal consolidation in the chest is suggestive of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
rationales.F12: Extensive reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates with focal consolidation in the chest is suggestive of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia or immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of fever, productive cough, and chest radiograph showing reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates are consistent with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, which is a common opportunistic infection in HIV-infected individuals with low CD4 counts.
